name: Rufous-crowned Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: Large songbird, brown above, white below, with orange crown, dark mask, and snow-white throat. Inhabits montane forests, though it frequently descends into foothills and lowlands during the winter.

name: Gold-naped Finch
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern india to southwestern china, southeastern tibet, and northern myanmar
description: A small dark finch of high mountain forests. Male is glossy black with a bright yellow nape.

name: Blue-and-white Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Halmahera, ternate, morotai, bacan, obi, and adjacent moluccas
description: A small kingfisher with bright azure-blue upperparts and a gleaming white underside. Female shows a diagnostic blue chest band.

name: Isabelline Bush-hen
rangeDescription: Lowlands of sulawesi
description: A large, long-legged rail with rich chestnut underparts, duller brown upperparts, a greenish bill, and greenish-yellow legs. Typically encountered in pairs or small groups within dense, rank grassland or thick scrub, in the lowlands and lower hills on Sulawesi.

name: Fulvous Owl
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern mexico (eastern oaxaca and chiapas) to el salvador
description: The southern counterpart to Barred Owl of the United States, this large brown-eyed owl occurs in highland forests from Oaxaca south to Honduras. Found in pine-oak and evergreen forest where it roosts at all levels, sometimes in fairly open situations.

name: Brown-banded Puffbird
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to northern amazonian brazil, southeastern peru, and northern bolivia
description: Large, black-and-white puffbird with a brown breast patch. In addition to its brown band, note the lack of a white eyebrow, present in other black-and-white puffbirds.

name: Western Nicator
rangeDescription: Senegal to northern angola, democratic republic of the congo, southern south sudan, uganda, and western tanzania
description: An unusual bushshrike-like bird with a heavy hooked bill, olive-green above and pale below with bold white spotting on the wings. The yellow corners of the tail can be conspicuous in flight.

name: Hooded Parrot
rangeDescription: Northern australia (northeastern northern territory)
description: A slender and long-tailed parrot restricted to a relatively small range in the Northern Territory, where it inhabits open woodlands. Male a striking turquoise color with black cap, yellow wings, rosy undertail coverts, and olive back.

name: Five-colored Barbet
rangeDescription: Western colombia (chocó) to far northwestern ecuador (esmeraldas)
description: Colorful barbet of lowland rainforest west of the Andes; scarce and declining in northwestern Ecuador, but more common in parts of southwestern Colombia. Male is black and yellow with red crown, white throat, and streaked flanks.
imageCreditName: Julio Calderón Birding Tour Guide Colombia🦉

name: Blue Petrel
rangeDescription: Islands in subantarctic southern oceans and islands off cape horn
description: Rather small, attractively patterned petrel of cold subantarctic waters; not seen from mainland. Sometimes accompanies ships, especially near breeding islands and with groups of similar-sized and superficially similar prions.

name: White-throated Greenbul
rangeDescription: Southwestern senegal eastward to far southern south sudan and uganda, southward to southern congo and western, northern, and eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A small, relatively long-billed greenbul found in the understory of disturbed forests and along forest edge. Often found in single- or multi-species flocks, flicking its wings and tail as it moves through the vegetation.

name: Patagonian Tinamou
rangeDescription: Savanna of southwestern argentina and southern chile
description: Large, cryptically patterned chickenlike bird of Patagonian grasslands with bushes and low shrubs. Scarce and rarely encountered.

name: Wakatobi White-eye
rangeDescription: Wakatobi (tukangbesi) islands, southeast of sulawesi
description: Bright yellowish white-eye found only on the Tukangbesi Islands off southeastern Sulawesi. Common to abundant in open coastal forest, forest edge, scrubby areas, gardens, plantations, and towns.

name: Gabela Bushshrike
rangeDescription: West-central angola (gabela escarpment)
description: A striking bushshrike with a chestnut crown and nape, blackish upperparts with a white wing-stripe, and entirely white underparts. A scarce species that skulks in pairs in the understory of secondary forest and farmbush, including coffee plantations, near Gabela along the Angolan escarpment.

name: Black Coucal
rangeDescription: Intra-african migrant south of the sahara
description: Small coucal of marshes, swamps, and wet grassland. Distinctive in breeding plumage: black with a rufous wing.

name: New Caledonian Whistler
rangeDescription: New caledonia
description: Orangey-yellow and olive whistler with a gray head and contrasting white throat. Female is much plainer, dull olive-brown with paler underparts and whitish throat.

name: African Skimmer
rangeDescription: Major rivers, lakes, and coasts of sub-saharan africa
description: Distinctive tern-like bird with long wings, a short tail, and a bizarre bill in which the upper mandible is shorter than the lower mandible. In slow flight, shows a very white underwing and a white stripe along the back of the upperwing.

name: Black-throated Grosbeak
rangeDescription: Humid forest and scrub of eastern brazil to paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: A largely grayish grosbeak found in the middle to upper levels of humid and montane forests. Males are slaty-blue overall with a black face and throat contrasting with a bright red bill.

name: Tatama Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of colombian andes (western antioquia southward to southwestern valle del cauca)
description: This typical “Scytalopus” tapaculo is found only in Colombia’s western Andes. Plumage is gray with a brown tinge to the rump and faint, rusty barring on the lower underparts.

name: Hartlaub's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Rocky hill country of southwestern angola to central namibia
description: Small francolin with an unusually long and downcurved bill. The male and female are very different: the male has a white eye-stripe and heavy streaking below, while the female has plain rufous underparts.
